draft.title: Evaporation and crystallisation
card: A solution is a solute dissolved in a solvent. When it is heated, the solvent turns into a gas and escapes. This is evaporation.
The solute does not evaporate with the solvent, so it is left behind as a solid. This separates a dissolved solid from its solvent.
the solid forming crystals as the solvent leaves the solution. The crystals are made of the solute.
Slow evaporation gives the particles more time to join in an orderly pattern, so larger crystals can form. Fast evaporation tends to give smaller crystals.
draft.remember: Evaporation removes the solvent and leaves the solute. Slower evaporation can give larger crystals.

a.q: A salt solution is heated in a dish until all the water is gone. What is left in the dish?
opts: Solid salt, which stayed behind as the water evaporated
Salt water, which has become more concentrated
Solid salt, which turned into water vapour and escaped
Nothing, because the salt and water both evaporated
a.why: The water evaporates and escapes as a gas, but the dissolved salt does not. It stays in the dish as a solid. Saying that both evaporate is tempting, but only the solvent leaves.
a.clue: Which part of the solution turns into a gas?

b.q: Jess leaves two identical dishes of copper sulfate solution. One sits in the sun, and one sits in a cool, shady spot. She wants the largest crystals. What should she do?
opts: Use the dish in the shade, where evaporation is slower
Use the dish in the sun, where evaporation is faster
Use the dish in the sun, because heat joins particles faster
Use either dish, because the crystals will be the same size
b.why: Slow evaporation gives the particles more time to settle into an orderly pattern, so larger crystals can form. The sunny dish loses its water faster, which tends to give smaller crystals.
b.clue: Think about which dish gives the particles more time.

a.best: Solid salt, which stayed behind as the water evaporated

b.best: Use the dish in the shade, where evaporation is slower
